Publication of the announcement of Albers's arrival at Black Mountain
The New York Herald Tribune publishes the article “German Professor to Go to Black Mt. College,” page 10.
The Alberses arrive in Asheville
Josef and Anni Albers, fresh from Berlin, arrive in Asheville to begin their new life. No decision was more decisive for the destiny of Black Mountain College.

The Asheville Citizen publishes a photo and an article on the recent arrival in town of the artists Josef and Anni Albers, from Berlin, who are joining the faculty of the brand-new Black Mountain College to head its art department.
The Asheville Citizen announces the Alberses' arrival

The paper announces that Josef and Frau Albers, from the Dessau Bauhaus, closed by Hitler's policies, are joining the faculty to create an art department, brought by the Museum of Modern Art in New York; the college is presented as the only one in the United States under the direct control of its faculty.
The Alberses' arrival photographed in the Asheville Citizen
North Carolina, Asheville area

The paper publishes a photo of the newly arrived Alberses, captioned “Germans to Teach Art Near Here.” The couple pose stiffly in a corner: Josef in jacket and tie, eyes averted, hands tightly clasped; Anni in fur, cloche, and veil, her gentle gaze turned toward the reader. They are fleeing the Nazi regime, leaving Berlin for a newly founded experimental school in rural Appalachia.
